title: Peddi Has Crossed ₹125 Crore in Three Days. Ram Charan Just Tied with RRR on BookMyShow.
excerpt: The sports drama is the fourth-fastest Indian film to sell 2 million tickets on BookMyShow — alongside RRR. The weekend could push it past ₹200 crore worldwide.
body:
There is a moment in every box office run where the numbers stop being numbers and start becoming a statement. **Peddi** hit that moment on Saturday afternoon, when its India net collection quietly crossed the ₹100 crore mark — three days into release, controversy swirling, and audiences still lining up.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=sF2dj7ycZvA</youtube>

The sports drama, directed by **Buchi Babu Sana** and starring **Ram Charan** as a village athlete who masters cricket, wrestling, and sprinting before the Indian government comes calling, has now accumulated approximately **₹125 crore net** at the Indian box office. Worldwide, the gross has blown past **₹200 crore**. For a film that opened on a Thursday against two other releases — **Bobby Deol**'s *Bandar* and **David Dhawan**'s farewell *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai* — that is not competition survived. That is competition erased.

## The BookMyShow Record That Matters

Here is the number that tells the real story: **2 million tickets sold on BookMyShow in 2.5 days**. That ties Peddi with *RRR* for the fourth-fastest film to reach the milestone on the platform. The only films ahead of it? *Pushpa 2: The Rule* (pre-release bookings alone), *Kalki 2898 AD* (1.5 days), and *Baahubali 2: The Conclusion* (2 days).

Read that list again. Every film on it is either a Rajamouli production or a spiritual successor to one. Peddi is neither. It is a sports film about a man from a village, scored by **A.R. Rahman**, and it is selling tickets at a pace that puts it in the company of the biggest spectacles Indian cinema has ever produced.

The peak-hour data is equally staggering. Peddi recorded **47,330 tickets sold in a single hour** on BookMyShow — fourth all-time, trailing only *Pushpa 2* (107,650), *Kalki 2898 AD* (95,710), and *Salaar* (54,760). The demand density during prime booking windows tells you something no review can: audiences are showing up with urgency.

## Day-by-Day: The Math

The opening day set the tone. Paid previews on Wednesday brought in **₹18.50 crore**, and Thursday proper delivered **₹51 crore net** — one of the biggest solo openings for any Telugu star. Friday dropped 47% to **₹26.90 crore**, which sounds steep until you remember it was a working day. Saturday brought the bounce: **₹28.85 crore** (early estimates), a 7.2% uptick that signals strong word-of-mouth holding through the weekend.

The Telugu version is doing the heavy lifting, as expected. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana generated roughly ₹25 crore gross on Saturday alone, with occupancy climbing to 60% during night shows. The Hindi version added ₹2.80 crore — modest, but growing. Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam are contributing smaller numbers, but the pan-India footprint is there.

> "Now you can't stop anyone. Every producer is of the opinion that 'Main kyun aage jaau?'" — Trade analyst Taran Adarsh on June 2026's crowded release calendar

## The Controversy Hasn't Slowed It Down

Peddi has not had a smooth ride. Director Buchi Babu Sana issued a public apology for the hypersexualised portrayal of **Janhvi Kapoor**'s character Achiyamma, and committed to editing certain scenes. The backlash was loud, sustained, and entirely justified. But the box office has responded to the film's other qualities — Ram Charan's physical transformation (the man looks like he was carved for this role), Rahman's score (atmospheric, percussive, impossible to forget), and a supporting cast that includes **Shiva Rajkumar**, **Jagapathi Babu**, **Divyenndu**, and **Boman Irani**.

The budget is reportedly in the **₹250–300 crore** range, which means Peddi is not yet in profit territory. But with Sunday expected to be the biggest single day of the run, and a full week of theatrical exclusivity ahead, the film is trending toward becoming Ram Charan's biggest solo hit — comfortably surpassing *Game Changer*'s lifetime numbers within its opening weekend.

## What It Means for Diaspora Viewers

Peddi is playing in theatres across **North America, the UK, the Middle East, and Australia**, with overseas gross already touching **₹42 crore**. If you are watching from abroad, this is the Telugu film of the summer — and possibly the only one that matters until *Cocktail 2* arrives on June 19. The Hindi dubbed version is expanding screens this weekend, so if your nearest theatre didn't have it on Thursday, check again.

Ram Charan is no longer the other half of *RRR*. He is the whole ticket.
